section: PROTOCOL §1.1 (targets), §4.1, §4.7 (frozen ladder, added to main 2026-09-1x by PRs #13–#15), §12 (nothing from memory) / SPEC §3.1
severity: **phase 2: thirteen new targets registered and launched under the reviewed discrete method (`run-discrete`, thresholds_v8); the PROTOCOL §4.7 ladder and §4.1 controller/real-space/reciprocal/validator agent structure are NOT what the driver implements — disclosed, not adopted**
description: Targets (operator's list, 2026-09-16): 9ARN 4QO4 8IS2 6CDX 1LZ9 9D5Y 1N7E 1V2X 1L6X 7DVR 6UDY 3DUT 9D5U. Every `targets/targets.yaml` value is the literal output of `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/<ID>` executed 2026-09-16 (saved with the run): all X-ray, 1.00–1.70 Å, structure factors released (`status_code_sf` REL); depositor R-work/R-free from `refine[0]`; free-set sizes 528 (4QO4, PROTOCOL §3.7 small-set note; header carries no cross-validation method) to 3587 (3DUT); 9D5Y/9D5U carry a 2 % free set; deposited refinement programs PHENIX (4), REFMAC (4), CNS (4), X-PLOR (1) — the CNS/X-PLOR entries' flag conventions are decided by `autoref/flags.py` from `_refln.status` / `pdbx_r_free_flag` at prep, and a file with no flag column halts that target (PROTOCOL §3.1) rather than generating one. Method: `scripts/onboard_target.sh` (fetch → prep → dossier → verify → noise-floor n=10 → baseline) then `scripts/run_dpdb.sh <T> --max-cycles 8` (correction, solvent, protein_altloc, adp_model ladder of SPEC_DPDB_RUNS §3; paired null control; site-restricted reciprocal step; R-gap, divergence and Metropolis rules of v8), orchestrated by `scripts/run_phase2.sh` (13 in parallel, `AUTOREF_NPROC` 24). No per-target `--refine-extra`: the standing 3QUE/3TC7 overrides are target-specific findings (D421, D496). Hydrogens: the deposited models are refined as deposited (mostly without riding H); PROTOCOL §4.1 as amended on main now permits riding H below 2.0 Å for all thirteen, and 3TC7's −0.011 credit (D488) says it can matter — H is a per-target paired experiment after the base runs (E028 pattern), not part of onboarding, because the ADP-weight optimiser's behaviour on H-bearing models needed a per-target fix (D491, D496). Disclosure: main's PROTOCOL §4.7 (L1–L10 with qFit at L3/L4, a standing `phenix.refine` block with `ordered_solvent=True` every macro-cycle and variants A/B, `solvent_model_select`, `zone_shift`, `backbone_split`) and §4.1 (four cooperating agents) describe a method the harness does not implement; the phase-2 runs follow SPEC_DPDB_RUNS as reviewed on 2026-09-08 (D480/D481). Whether to build the ladder is an operator decision; this row records that the two documents now disagree and which one the runs followed.

section: CLAUDE.md (edit local, run remote) / SPEC_DPDB_RUNS §6 (running it on the pod)
severity: **operating error, no data lost: `scripts/onboard_target.sh` was edited (the exit-code report, PR #18) while eleven instances of it were running on the pod; bash reads a script incrementally, so each instance failed as soon as its noise-floor stage returned (6CDX 05:01Z, 4QO4 05:05Z, 7DVR 05:10Z, the rest as their floors finish), before `baseline` and before its run was launched**
description: Symptom: STATUS ends at `noise_floor ok`, no `baseline start`, no baseline.log; `phase2.log` says `onboarding FAILED — no run launched`. The live sync pushes every local save to `/home/dev/workspace` at once, so a local edit is an edit of the running file. Nothing scientific is affected: the `noise_floor` rows were written before the failure (6CDX σ_select 0.000548, σ_report 0.000634, n 10), every onboarding stage is idempotent (fetch reuses, prep verifies checksums, noise floor resumes finished seeds) and no refinement had been judged. Recovery: `run_phase2.sh --targets "6CDX 4QO4 7DVR"` relaunched at 05:13Z; a one-off reaper (`/home/dev/runs/phase2_reaper.sh`, logged in `phase2_reaper.log`) relaunches each of 8IS2 1LZ9 9D5Y 1N7E 1V2X 6UDY 3DUT 9D5U once its STATUS reads `noise_floor ok` and its original process is gone; 9ARN and 1L6X (relaunched 04:33Z, after the edit) are unaffected. Rule added to CLAUDE.md: never edit a shell script that is running on the pod — the sync makes the edit live; launchers should copy the scripts they run to a per-launch snapshot (to be added to `run_phase2.sh` once its current instances have exited, since that file is running too).

severity: **harness fix: the PDB-REDO baseline (baseline 3) no longer halts a target when its refinement writes no model; the failure becomes a `defects` row, and a model refused for malformed HELIX/SHEET annotation is retried once with that annotation removed and the edit recorded**
description: Found on 1V2X (relaunched onboarding, 05:56Z): `phenix.refine` refused PDB-REDO's `1v2x_final.cif` with `Sorry: Bad helix length. Check HELIX records. HELIX 1 1 ARG A 2 ARG A 2` — the file carries 49 `_struct_conf` rows, five of them one-residue helices (the deposited 1V2X.cif has 10 rows and none); `stages/baseline.py::_one` then crashed on `Path(None)` and the target's onboarding stopped before its run. Baseline 3 is a comparison the report quotes, not an input to any decision, so its failure must not block the target (the stage already wrote a defects row when the PDB-REDO file was absent). Fix: `_one(required=False)` for the PDB-REDO baseline returns `model: None` + the phenix message and writes `defects`; the input and re-refined baselines stay required and raise after recording. Retry: when the message names the helix records, `_strip_secondary_structure` (gemmi; removes `_struct_conf`, `_struct_conf_type`, `_struct_sheet_range`) writes `<model>.no_ss.cif` next to the run and the refinement is repeated on it once, with `input_edit.json` and the `input_edit` field of the result saying what was removed — the annotation is metadata, not coordinates, and at 1.5 Å no secondary-structure restraints are derived from it. No other target's baseline failed (`"ok": false` appears only in 1V2X's). Tests: `tests/test_baseline_failures.py` (4). 1V2X relaunched after the fix.

severity: **finding, no rule changed: for the legacy (CNS/REFMAC/X-PLOR-era) phase-2 targets the standard noise floor — ten seeds of one 5-macro-cycle re-refinement of the deposited model — measures convergence variance, not test-set noise, and its credit bar is unreachable; recommendation: a versioned convergence step before the floor, then repeat the legacy runs**
description: Evidence (E034/E034b on 1LZ9, `runs/1LZ9/experiments/e034*_nf_converged/result.json`, ten seeds each, thresholds_v8, no `noise_floor` row written): standing floor σ_select 0.005895 (bar −0.0118), σ_full 0.005568, mean select 0.2872; from the run's one-pass baseline σ_select 0.004219, σ_report 0.006099, mean 0.2828; from the run's six-pass final base σ_select **0.001665**, σ_full 0.001332, mean 0.2774 — 3.5× smaller, with σ_gap unchanged (0.0018 → 0.0020). The model itself moved 0.2941 → 0.2789 → 0.2739 on select over its first passes. Consequences for the phase-2 verdicts: 1LZ9 (σ 0.0059), 6UDY (0.0087), 1L6X (0.0055) and 1V2X (0.0008 but −0.12 on its annealing arm) ended with nothing or little credited because no local change can clear a bar set by convergence spread; 6UDY's −0.019 select gains only cleared a −0.017 bar because its whole model was still settling (its first such cycle was refused by the R-gap gate at +3.0σ_gap, D495, the second credited). A second class of wide bars is genuine: small free sets (9ARN 771 → σ_select 0.0054 against an analytic 0.011; 4QO4 528 → 0.0019; 7DVR 882 → 0.0010). Not changed here: the standing rows, thresholds, or any verdict — a floor is a measurement of the judging protocol's input (D491), and changing that input for a target is a D-row decision the operator should own for thirteen targets at once. Recommendation: `thresholds_v9` with `noise_floor.converge_passes` (or `refine.baseline_macro_cycles`, cf. E030's 15) applied to the baseline before the floor is measured; re-measure the floor from that model for every phase-2 target (`autoref noise-floor --model … --label converged`, which replaces the judging row, D488); repeat the legacy runs from their standing records; quote every phase-2 gain against the mean of that floor, not against the single baseline re-refinement (1LZ9's baseline record sits 0.014 above its own second pass).

severity: **phase-2 results, ten of thirteen runs finished (3DUT, 9D5U, 9D5Y still running); every number verified with the independent scorer (`runs/verify_20260917/`, agreement with the ledger ≤ 0.0013) and quoted on the frozen inherited flags**
description: Deliverables moved on four targets — 6CDX 0.2258 → **0.1716** full (re-refinement alone 0.1901; −0.0184 beyond it, 37σ_full; 2 credits: sub-floor waters removed, alternate conformations at A5, A34, B20 and a water added; 589 → 630 atoms); 1N7E 0.2746 → **0.2447** (re-refinement 0.2474; −0.0027, 3.0σ; 1 credit, five waters removed); 4QO4 0.3128 → **0.3243** (re-refinement 0.3502; −0.0259 beyond it, 6.4σ, 3 credits incl. the `rescale_bulk_solvent` escape rung — but still +0.0114 above the deposited model recomputed: phenix's default re-refinement of the CNS model costs 0.037 and the run recovers 0.026 of it; PROTOCOL §6: a program artifact, reported as such); 6UDY 0.2592 → **0.2479** (re-refinement 0.2567; −0.0088, 1.1σ of a 0.0087 floor; 1 credit that recovered cycle-0 drift, D506; report half worse than the baseline's, D508). Six targets credited nothing and keep their re-refined baselines: 1LZ9 0.2822 (deposited 0.2738 is better — REFMAC model degraded by phenix re-refinement), 7DVR 0.2873, 1V2X 0.2354, 9ARN 0.2962, 1L6X 0.2390, 8IS2 0.2668 (each within ±1.3σ of its re-refinement mean). Method statistics over the 40 paired cycles so far: 7 credited, 5 regressed and bisected (culprits found in 2, interactions in 3), 28 within noise; Metropolis (D499) kept 8 within-noise-but-worse candidates in 5 runs, all recorded with p and u, none credited, drift guard never fired, no deliverable moved because of one; 17 escape rungs failed, 1 credited; 1 R-gap refusal (6UDY c001, +3.0σ_gap on a −0.019 select gain); promotion refused at 4QO4 c001–c003 and 9D5U c001 (credited best base not better than the standing record, D499) and at 6UDY c006–c007 (deliverable gap bound, D495); 953 change rows. Caveats that travel with the table: D506 (legacy floors are convergence variance), D507 (PROTOCOL §4.4 replaced k·σ during the campaign; nothing re-judged yet), D508 (report-half promotion bound added after 6UDY), 9D5U/9D5Y recompute 0.02–0.03 above their headers (D008-type).
